papers.titleEn: “Lab-on-Double Confinement-Pipette Tip”: CDsCu/Mn@MPDA-Driven Portable Intelligent Sensor for In-Situ Rapid Detection of Pesticide Residues
papers.abstract: The development of high specificity, ultrasensitive, and portable detection technologies is conducive to monitoring pesticide residues in the environment, thereby promoting the scientific use of pesticides. Here, a dual-confined sensitization "lab-on-pipette tip" was developed for colorimetric-photothermal in-situ detection of carbosulfan by encapsulating nanomaterials within the hydrogel matrix on a pipette tip. As the signal transduction core, an interfacial-enhanced mesoporous polydopamine was loaded with dual-metal carbon dots (CDsCu/Mn@MPDA) to mimic high-efficiency peroxidase activity. The synergy between the bimetallic sites lowered the energy barrier for the reduction of H2O2, generating abundant hydroxyl radicals. Crucially, the reducing sulfur species generated from acidified carbosulfan inhibit the activity of CDsCu/Mn@MPDA by triggering radical-scavenging reactions, generating target concentration-dependent signals. Furthermore, CDsCu/Mn@MPDA was encapsulated in the hydrogel and gelled at the pipette tip to construct an integrated platform. The double-confinement effect enhanced reaction-component contact efficiency, resulting in a 40-fold compression of the linear response range for carbosulfan residue detection. The sensing platform exhibited a response range of 0-1200 µM in solution. Strikingly, this range was compressed to 0-30 µM within the spatially confined microcavity. This on-demand tunable range platform slashes per-assay costs by ∼99.7% vs liquid chromatography mass spectrometry, bridging the lab-to-field gap for environmental sensing.
papers.filename: Yingwang Ye, ACS Sens., 2026, “Lab-on-Double Confinement-Pipette Tip” CDsCu Mn@MPDA-Driven Portable Intelligent Sensor for In-Situ Rapid Detection of Pesticide Residues

papers.titleEn: Visual Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Leafy Greens Using an AsCas12f-Split-G-Quadruplex Sensor
papers.abstract: Abstract Foodborne viruses are responsible for a substantial burden of disease worldwide, with fresh produce serving as the most abundant vehicle for transmission. However, rapid detection in solid produce, such as leafy greens, remains underdeveloped, as conventional methods often require labor-intensive sample preparation and specialized instrumentation. Herein, we present a colorimetric CRISPR-split-G4 biosensor for rapid viral surveillance in leafy greens that combines reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA), AsCas12f-mediated trans-cleavage, and a modular split-G-quadruplex (split-G4) reporter system. In this system, target recognition activates the trans-cleavage activity of AsCas12f, resulting in degradation of a blocker strand and subsequent assembly of a catalytically active G4-hemin DNAzyme that generates a visible signal easily detectable by the naked eye. Using norovirus as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, enabling reliable detection of viral particles with minimal instrumentation. To evaluate practical applicability, the assay was coupled with a simplified leaf-disk extraction workflow and successfully applied to contaminated romaine lettuce and baby spinach samples without requiring viral nucleic acid purification. The platform achieved detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. From sample processing to visual readout, the entire assay was completed in approximately 2 h. By integrating isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based target recognition, and instrument-free signal generation into a streamlined workflow, this strategy provides a promising platform for decentralized food safety monitoring and establishes a flexible framework for the on-site detection of viral pathogens in complex food matrices.
papers.filename: Juhong Chen, ACS Sens., 2026, Visual Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Leafy Greens Using an AsCas12f-Split-G-Quadruplex Sensor

papers.titleEn: Crystalline NiO:N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract The buried hole-selective contact in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is expected to transport holes through its bulk while also templating a defect-free self-assembled monolayer (SAM). A crystalline, vacuum-deposited nitrogen-doped NiO (NiO:N) film deterministically templates a uniformly anchored SAM, while the reactive-atmosphere N2/O2 ratio used during pulsed laser deposition (PLD) simultaneously programs bulk hole density and interfacial anchoring chemistry. Nitrogen incorporation is proposed to act as a shallow acceptor that generates Ni3+ states and raises p-type conductivity, whereas the dense, pinhole-free template enforces uniform SAM coverage, fully suppressing the underlying substrate signal and minimizing surface hydroxyl groups relative to discontinuous nanoparticle films. Consequently, NiO:N/SAM-based PSCs achieve a 6.2% relative increase in power conversion efficiency (PCE) over pristine NiO nanoparticles, reaching one of the highest reported performances for vacuum-deposited NiO-based PSCs, with improved thermal and operational stability. These results establish reactive-atmosphere NiO:N as a general, scalable platform for hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Yun Seog Lee, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Crystalline NiO N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T–Hg2+–T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.
